questions.q: Which framework defines the four-phase incident response lifecycle this course is built around?
options: The OWASP Top Ten
The CVSS scoring framework
ISO 27001, the information security management standard
NIST SP 800-61, the Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
questions.explain: NIST SP 800-61 is the real framework incident response plans, tabletop exercises, and job postings are written around.

questions.q: What are the four phases of the NIST incident response lifecycle, in order?
options: Detection, Response, Recovery, Reporting
Alerting, Triage, Escalation, Closure
Preparation, Detection & Analysis, Containment/Eradication/Recovery, Post-Incident Activity
Planning, Execution, Monitoring, Shutdown
questions.explain: Those four phases, in that order, make up the NIST SP 800-61 lifecycle.

questions.q: Why is the lifecycle drawn as a cycle rather than a straight line?
options: Because SOCs are legally required to repeat each phase twice
It's drawn as a cycle purely for visual style, with no practical meaning
Because Detection & Analysis must run before Preparation every time
Post-Incident Activity feeds lessons learned back into Preparation, improving the next incident response
questions.explain: The arrow from Post-Incident Activity back to Preparation represents real gaps a team found getting fixed before the next incident.

questions.q: Which phase is where an alert gets formally confirmed as a real incident, building directly on the triage process taught in SOC Operations & SIEM Fundamentals?
options: Preparation
Containment, Eradication & Recovery
Detection & Analysis
Post-Incident Activity
questions.explain: Detection & Analysis is where triage-level validation happens at incident scale, confirming an alert is genuinely an incident.

questions.q: A SOC discovers, after resolving an incident, that an alert sat untouched for 40 minutes because the on-call rotation was never clearly documented. Which phase captures that finding, and where does the fix for it belong?
options: Containment, Eradication & Recovery captures the finding; no fix is needed
Preparation captures the finding; the fix belongs in Post-Incident Activity
Post-Incident Activity captures the finding; the fix belongs in Preparation
Detection & Analysis captures the finding; the fix belongs in Containment
questions.explain: Post-Incident Activity is the lessons-learned review, and findings like this feed back into Preparation to close the loop.
